After breakfast, set off on a six-hour city tour with an English-speaking guide.

Begin at Praia Vermelha, the Red Beach. From here, a cable car takes you up to Urca Hill, where a broad viewing platform looks out over Rio. A second cable car takes you to the top of Sugarloaf Mountain. From the summit you can see Copacabana, Ipanema, Leme, Guanabara Bay, the Rio–Niterói Bridge, Niterói itself, the surrounding mountains, islands in the ocean and the Christ the Redeemer statue on Corcovado.

After coming back down, continue to the historic centre. You will see old churches and monasteries, colonial-era buildings, the Sambadrome where Carnival is held each year, the Cathedral of Saint Sebastian and the Municipal Theatre.

Then head to the foot of Corcovado. A small train climbs through the tropical forest to the upper station, a few minutes’ walk from Christ the Redeemer. Corcovado stands at 704 metres. The statue is 30 metres tall, excluding its seven-metre pedestal.

The viewing platform offers one of Rio de Janeiro’s best-known views. After the tour, return to your hotel with your guide.
Aerial view of the city, racecourse and ocean in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: City and coastal panorama from the mountain

Have breakfast at the hotel, then transfer to the airport and fly to Campo Grande. On arrival, continue to the Pantanal.

The Pantanal lies in central South America. This vast natural area is home to a wide variety of plants and animals. Its rivers, lakes and wetlands provide habitats for many birds, reptiles and mammals.

Check in at your hotel or lodge. Here you can swap city sights for time in nature: listen to the sounds of the forest, watch birds and butterflies, photograph wildlife and relax away from the big cities.
